I am 65 years old, I have farmed for 40 years in Quzhou, and I finished middle school. My family has six people, some of them work off-farm in the county town, so I manage the 10.1 mu myself with help from my wife. I keep 7 mu for wheat and summer maize because that is my grain base and the double-cropping works well on my well-irrigated land. The other 3.1 mu grows cotton for extra cash. I do not try new tricks. I watch Lao Zhang across the road and Old Wang to the east. If their wheat looks good, I copy them.

For the wheat already in the ground since last October, I use an improved variety, the same one I have planted for five years. Before sowing, I rotary-tilled the 7 mu and put down one 50-kilogram bag of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base. At green-up in March, I topdress half a bag of urea per mu, 25 kilograms. Wheat needs water, so from my well I will irrigate three times: once at jointing in late March, once at heading in late April, and once at grain filling in mid-May if the sky stays dry. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids when the weather warms, and once for rust before the ears fill. Last year I got 450 kilograms per mu, and I expect the same this year if no disaster hits.

For summer maize on the same 7 mu, I plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I used to plough everything, but now I sow no-till straight into the wheat stubble like everyone else; it saves diesel and time, and the seedlings come up fine. At sowing, I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu into the seed-furrow. When the plants reach my knee, I broadcast 25 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate twice from the well: once at the big-flare stage in July, and once at grain filling in August if the rains fail. I spray twice for armyworm and leaf blight. I expect 550 kilograms per mu.

For cotton on the 3.1 mu, I plough deep in April with my small tractor because cotton roots need loose soil down deep. I plant hybrid cotton seed. I spread one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and when the first buds show I topdress with 20 kilograms of urea plus 15 kilograms of potassium chloride per mu. Cotton sucks up potassium; without it the bolls drop on the ground. I irrigate three times: at budding, at flowering, and at peak boll in August. I spray pesticide four times, mainly for bollworm in July and August. Last year I harvested 250 kilograms of seed cotton per mu; this year I hope for 260.

Fertilizer costs hurt. A bag of urea is over 100 yuan now. But I saw what happened to Old Wang two years ago when he cut his wheat fertilizer to save money: his yield dropped to 300 kilograms per mu. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will spend the money.
